hits.tldr: Theme variables compile to CSS custom properties for use in stylesheets.
Tailwind CSS imports default theme variables for colors, fonts, shadows, and spacing via layer declarations.
Use the prefix option to namespace Tailwind CSS classes and variables to avoid naming conflicts.
Prefixed classes appear at the start of class names, theme variables are configured without prefix but generated CSS includes it.
Use the `inline` option when theme variables reference other variables to avoid CSS resolution issues.

hits.tldr: Tailwind CSS imports default theme variables for colors, fonts, shadows, and spacing via layer declarations.
Prefixed classes appear at the start of class names, theme variables are configured without prefix but generated CSS includes it.
Use the prefix option to namespace Tailwind CSS classes and variables to avoid naming conflicts.
Disable Tailwind preflight by omitting the preflight.css import while keeping theme and utilities imports.
Use the `static` theme option to generate all CSS variables in output, not just used ones.

content.text:
Not entirely safe without a prefix, but the docs offer a fix: the `prefix()` option.

- With `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);`, the generated theme variables get a prefix too (e.g. `--tw-color-red-500`). That includes built-in ones such as the ones `rounded-lg` uses. You keep writing `@theme` variables without the prefix (`src/docs/upgrade-guide.mdx`, "Changes from v3 › Using a prefix"; `src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Managing style conflicts › Using the prefix option").
- The upgrade guide says the prefix on generated variables is there "to avoid conflicts with any existing variables in your project".
- The catch is that utility classes are prefixed as well (`tw:rounded-lg`). The docs don't offer a way to prefix only the variables.
- Without a prefix, `--color-*` in your CSS can clash with a user's variables of the same name. The docs say nothing more about this risk.
- By default only used variables are emitted (`src/docs/theme.mdx`, "Generating all CSS variables"). This narrows the exposure, but the docs don't promise it removes the risk.
